questions.q: Why did Blake Mycoskie choose a for-profit company over a charity for TOMS?
a: A business would provide a steadier supply of shoes than donations
Charities were not allowed to operate in Argentina
Investors refused to fund any kind of charity
A company would let him keep all the profits
questions.why: The overview says a profitable business would not depend on the fluctuating generosity of donors.

questions.q: How did Mycoskie deal with his fear of starting the company?
a: He wrote down each fear and what would happen if it came true
He asked friends to talk him out of starting it
He avoided thinking about the risks until launch day
He took a course on the shoe industry first
questions.why: Lesson 1 says listing his fears and their consequences showed him the worst case was survivable.

questions.q: What does the summary say is the key to a simple business?
a: Choose one thing and do it as well as you can
Offer as many products as possible to reach more people
Copy the model of the biggest competitor
Wait for enough money before starting
questions.why: Lesson 2 says focusing on one thing saves money and makes the model easier for investors to grasp.

questions.q: How did the TOMS team keep costs down at the beginning?
a: They worked from the founder’s living room and reused materials
They rented a large office in the city center
They outsourced everything to overseas factories
They hired a big staff before launch
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the team working from a living room and the author recycling other people’s business cards.

questions.q: Why does the summary say giving is good business?
a: It gives customers a story they want to share with others
It guarantees lower production costs
It removes the need for any marketing at all
It lets companies avoid paying taxes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says people connect emotionally with the story of giving and become fans who spread it themselves.
